To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA immunization with the EHV-1 gene for gD induced specific antibody and cell-mediated responses and protected mice against a respiratory challenge with EHV1.

1) DNA-mediated immunization with the EHV-1 envelope glycoprotein, gD, was able to elicit a specific antibody response and a Th1-type cell-mediated immune response in mice, 2) EHV-1 DNA-immunized mice were protected against a respiratory challenge with EHV, and 3) DNA vaccination was able to ellicit protection against EHV infection in a murine respiratory model.

DNA immunization of a mouse model with a gene for the glycoprotein D from equine herpesv1 (EHV1) induces a Th1 immune response, which protects the animal from a respiratory infection with the same virus.

the development of a DNA vaccine against equine herpesviral infection.
the development of a vaccine to control respiratory disease caused by EHV-1.
the development of a DNA-based vaccine for the control of respiratory disease caused by EHV-1.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA-mediated immunization with EHV- 1 gD can induce a protective immune response against respiratory challenge with EHV 1.

The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA-mediated immunization can induce protective immunity against a respiratory virus in a small animal model.
